TimestampMs.description: A point in time: milliseconds since the Unix epoch (UTC).

DurationMs.description: A length of time or a position in milliseconds.

Cursor.description: An opaque pagination cursor. Pass it back unchanged to get the next page. Never build or parse it.

Limit.description: The maximum number of items in one page (1–100). A page can hold fewer items even when more exist.

NextCursor.description: The cursor for the next page, or null when this is the last page.

ThumbnailUrl.description: An absolute HTTPS URL of the largest available artwork image, or null when there is none.

Scope.description: A permission an app can be granted. See "Scopes" for what each one allows and what the user sees.

AppId.description: A stable reverse-DNS app id: lowercase, at least three dot-separated labels, at most 128 characters, for example `com.example.mybar`. The `dev.sonolith.` prefix is reserved.

ApiVersionRequest.description: The API version the client was written for, as `MAJOR.MINOR`, for example `1.0`.

ApiVersion.description: The full API version Sonolith implements, as semantic version `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`.

Empty.description: An empty object: the method succeeded and has nothing to return.

ErrorData.description: The `data` member of every Sonolith error. `name` and `reason` are always present; the other members appear only on the errors that define them.

name.description: The error name, for example `PermissionDenied`. Match on this or on the numeric code.

reason.description: A machine-readable detail, for example `cursorExpired`, or null. See "Error reasons".

retryAfterMs.description: RateLimited, RegistrationDenied, Unavailable: wait at least this long before trying again.

scope.description: PermissionDenied: the scope the method or topic needs.

requestId.description: RegistrationPending: the id of the pending request; its outcome arrives as `registration.resolved`.

expiresAt.description: RegistrationPending: when the pending request expires.

supported.description: UnsupportedVersion: the API major versions Sonolith supports, for example `["1"]`.

path.description: InvalidParams: a JSON Pointer to the offending parameter, for example `/items/0/id`.
